21. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343 has laid down the general principles relating to compensation in injury cases and held:
"6.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
MACT No. 78/2021 Ahmad vs. Mohd. Hasam & Ors.

entities.text: MACT No. 78/2021 Ahmad vs. Mohd. Hasam & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page No. 7 of 19 (iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life."

The petitioner, in his evidence by way of affidavit, has claimed that he spent 5 lacs on medicines and treatment.
The treatment record and medical bills of the petitioner (Ex. PW2/1) shows that he received most of his treatment at Nidaan Hospital & Trauma Centre, Sohna, which is a private hospital.
The original medical bills and corresponding receipts placed on record by the petitioner amount to 1,91,546/-.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to 1,91,546/- towards medicines and treatment.

23. The petitioner, in his evidence by way of affidavit, has further claimed that he spent 50,000/-
on conveyance and Rs.50,000/- on special diet.
However, no documentary proof has been placed on record in support of the said claims.
Nonetheless, having regard to the fact that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries , it can reasonably be inferred that he must have incurred expenses on special diet as well as on conveyance.
Accordingly, a sum of 20,000/- is awarded towards special diet and 20,000/- towards conveyance.
